title: Normalized completed regular pullback units are quasi-isomorphisms for arbitrary scheme maps
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its completed integral coefficient sheaves $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and finite quotient sheaves $B_{W,m}$ of positive exponent $m+1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Write $U_W=R_W[0]$ for the regular coefficient complex and $P_f$ for its specified strict pullback quotient tower, with actual Roos endomorphism $1-T$ [def-weil-constant-weil-structure, def-pur-integral-operation-complex-models]. Let $\eta:U_X\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$ be a chain map. Suppose that, for every nonnegative $m$ and every pro-etale object $V$ of $Y$, the degree-zero $m$th unshifted cone projection sends the regular section one over $f^*V$ to the actual adjunction image of the reduced regular section one over $V$ [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback]. Suppose also that the shifted cone component is zero in every degree. Then $Q(\eta)$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of $R_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: At every positive quotient, the ordinary ringed-site pullback of the regular coefficient module is canonically the target regular module by multiplication. The base-change functor preserves the terminal object, hence is final, so Mathlib pullbackObjUnitToUnit is invertible. Its transpose sends the regular generator one to one. Compare this with the existing exact single-complex and finite reduction identifications; the finite pulled regular complex is therefore the target quotient regular complex, with its actual adjunction generator identified with one. This uses no isomorphism hypothesis on the scheme map.

proof.text: Compose each specified unit projection with its regular-module isomorphism. Naturality of the finite adjunction and the generator equation show that this composite sends one to the actual quotient projection of one. The source is the regular module in degree zero, so linearity and its terminal-section generator determine the entire map. Thus these are the actual quotient projections. Compatibility of the unit projections and of quotient projections, together with epimorphy of the quotient projections, proves naturality of the level isomorphisms. They form an isomorphism of whole towers. Transport the completed coefficient limit cone, embedded by the exact limit-preserving single-complex functor, across this tower isomorphism.

proof.text: The quotient tower transitions are epic, as proved by the existing coefficient tower calculation. Apply milnor_epimorphic to get epimorphy of one minus shift on its product. The single-complex product comparison and the whole-tower isomorphism preserve this epimorphy. The ordinary limit cone is the kernel of one minus shift by the universal properties of the product and limit. Consequently its inclusion and the Roos endomorphism form a short exact sequence of complexes. The proved kernel-to-shifted-mapping-cone comparison shows that the corresponding cocone lift with zero shifted component is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: The given chain map eta and the constructed candidate have the same finite regular generators and zero shifted component. The existing normalized_chainUnit_unique theorem, which is valid for arbitrary scheme maps, identifies them. Hence eta is precisely the quasi-isomorphism from the preceding step. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms makes its image invertible. Empty schemes cause no exception: all regular-section and limit arguments apply to their zero module sheaves as well.

theorem normalizedChainUnit_isIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (η : constantWeilIntegralComplex l E X ⟶
        (integralOperationsPullbackComplexFunctor l E f).obj
          (constantWeilIntegralComplex l E Y))
    (hη :
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (V : Y.ProEt),
        ((η.f 0 ≫
          (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
            (constantWeilPullbackRoosEndomorphism l E f)).f 0 ≫
          (Pi.π (fun j ↦ (constantWeilPullbackTower l E f).obj (op j)) m).f 0).val.app
            (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)))
          (constantWeilUnitSection l E X ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) =
        integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E f m
          (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y m).obj
            (constantWeilIntegralComplex l E Y)).X 0) V
          (constantWeilReducedUnitSection l E Y m V)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, η.f i ≫
        (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd
          (constantWeilPullbackRoosEndomorphism l E f)).v i (i - 1) (by omega) = 0)) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map η)
